title: Vector Databases
description: Explore ANN algorithms (HNSW, IVF, PQ), Pinecone/Weaviate/Milvus architecture, semantic search pipelines, embedding dimensionality tradeoffs, and hybrid search combining vectors with keywords.

segments.text: Traditional databases search by exact match — find rows where name equals 'Alice'. Vector databases search by similarity — find items semantically similar to this query. An embedding model converts text, images, or code into high-dimensional vectors. Semantically similar items have nearby vectors. This enables search by meaning, not keywords.

Exact nearest neighbor search in one billion vectors is impossibly slow — O(N) comparisons per query. Approximate Nearest Neighbor algorithms trade a small accuracy loss for massive speed gains. With ninety-five percent recall, queries that would take minutes complete in milliseconds. The three dominant ANN algorithms: HNSW, IVF, and Product Quantization.

HNSW — Hierarchical Navigable Small World — builds a multi-layer graph. The top layer has a few long-range connections for fast navigation. Lower layers have denser local connections for precision. Query traversal: start at the top, greedily follow the closest neighbor, then descend to the next layer. This achieves sub-millisecond queries on millions of vectors. Pinecone uses HNSW internally.

IVF — Inverted File Index — partitions vectors into clusters using k-means. At query time, only the nearest clusters are searched. Product Quantization compresses vectors by splitting them into subvectors and quantizing each — a 768-dimensional vector becomes sixty-four bytes instead of three thousand seventy-two. IVF-PQ combines both: clustered search on compressed vectors. Milvus uses this extensively.

You have one billion vectors of dimension 768. Storing them uncompressed takes three terabytes of memory. HNSW gives the best query speed but requires the index in memory. IVF-PQ reduces memory by eight times but with lower recall. How do you choose?
segments.thought_prompt: HNSW (fast, 3TB RAM) vs IVF-PQ (8x smaller, lower recall) for 1B vectors. How do you decide?

segments.text: Pinecone: fully managed, serverless vector database. Handles indexing, scaling, and replication transparently. Weaviate: open-source, supports modules for vectorization — bring your own embeddings or use built-in models. Milvus: open-source, designed for billion-scale vector search, supports GPU-accelerated indexing. Each targets a different operational maturity and scale.

A semantic search pipeline: user query goes to an embedding model — same model used for indexing. The query embedding is sent to the vector database. The database returns the K nearest vectors with their document IDs. Those IDs fetch the original documents from a document store. Total latency: fifty to one hundred milliseconds including embedding computation.

Embedding dimensionality is a key tradeoff. Higher dimensions — 1536 from OpenAI — capture more semantic nuance but require more storage, memory, and compute. Lower dimensions — 384 from MiniLM — are faster and cheaper but less accurate. For most applications, 768 dimensions provide the optimal balance. Dimensionality reduction via PCA or Matryoshka embeddings can further optimize.

Hybrid search combines vector similarity with keyword matching. A query for 'python error handling' should find documents semantically about error handling AND containing the keyword 'python'. Use reciprocal rank fusion: compute vector similarity scores and BM25 keyword scores independently, then combine ranks. This outperforms either method alone by ten to twenty percent in relevance.

Design a semantic search system for a knowledge base with ten million documents, supporting both natural language queries and exact keyword matches, with sub-one-hundred-millisecond latency and real-time document updates.
segments.thought_prompt: Design semantic search for 10M documents: NL queries + keywords, sub-100ms, real-time updates.

segments.text: Vector databases enable search by meaning using ANN algorithms — HNSW for speed, IVF-PQ for memory efficiency. The semantic search pipeline converts queries to embeddings and finds nearest neighbors. Hybrid search combining vectors with keywords gives the best relevance. The Staff-level insight: choose your embedding model and dimensionality based on your accuracy-cost tradeoff, and always benchmark with your actual data.
